title: fix: deliver completed replies while Claude background research continues
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed Claude CLI answers remaining invisible while native background research continues, including when raw previews and block streaming are disabled.

## User Impact

Completed answers reach the channel through normal reply policies and hooks without waiting for every continuation. Already delivered segments are not replayed; definitely unsent segments retain their recovery path. Background work keeps its existing admitted turn and permissions. This does not shorten the research or make the turn available to a different caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

Answer delivery and transport completion are separate boundaries. The runtime identifies held results, and the parser exposes completed answers to the existing reply pipeline. Stable segment identities survive early delivery, coalescing, deferred-tail recovery, and final settlement.

Review repairs also preserve independent replies with shared prefixes, suppress repeated result acknowledgments without losing earlier text, require a real terminal result, keep the complete final preview, and prevent completed answers from overtaking earlier presentation or remaining below a coalescing threshold.

## Evidence

- **288 focused tests passed** in secretless AWS isolation (Linux, Node 24.19.0). Coverage includes native stdio continuation authority/cancellation, parser/result boundaries, normal CLI reply delivery with previews and block streaming off, directives/silent/media policy, final dedupe, definite-send failure recovery, coalescing, deferred tails, and delayed-commentary ordering in both progress modes.
- Red/green regressions reproduced prefix clipping, missing early delivery, coalesced replay/lost tail recovery, an interim-only stream incorrectly succeeding, buffered completed answers, and completed replies overtaking prior commentary.
- Independent whole-candidate autoreview explicitly included **P0–P3** and completed **scoped-clean**. The substantive ClawSweeper segment-identity finding is addressed with coalescing and deferred-tail regressions.
- [Focused verification and per-file costs](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cd0b40bc8e9de1d051b650807b25171c). That run's subsequent typecheck exposed two callback typing mismatches; those were corrected without changing runtime behavior.
- [Changed-file validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_505a0e42b27e017e3b768cd9104fad72) passed core, all core-test graphs, extension, and extension-test typechecks plus the preceding guards. It then identified lint violations; the follow-up fixes those without suppressions or behavior changes. Core lint subsequently passed, and the remaining extension parameter-reassignment issue is corrected.
- A broader PR-head replay of the hosted shard specification passed **536 tests across 37 files**. The earlier hosted SQLite teardown error was not reproduced by that replay. Its owning fixture cleanup was independently fixed on main in [#154898](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154898), commit `112fcfbd81dbce4ff707b241a423bf1b64b2c3f9`. The conflict-resolution merge retains that canonical file byte-for-byte, rather than carrying a duplicate fixture implementation or experiment in this PR. Production cleanup guards, retries, and timeouts are unchanged.
- A final isolated follow-up probe was **blocked before execution by GitHub HTTP 429 during source checkout** ([run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_50ca988741c084b595c185a35092c347)); it is not counted as passing. The follow-up delta passed independent P3 review. The earlier main merge resolved that fixture conflict while preserving contributor ancestry. A later ancestry-preserving refresh incorporates the landed hosted-lifecycle synchronization repair described below. Fresh current-head secretless fork CI and applicable reviews remain required before landing.

### CI readiness-failure investigation

The [head `2a7bf94` CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35625668678) failed three groups: three main-session recovery readiness assertions and nine approval-readiness assertions, with five subsequent observer-closure errors. The named sanitization, identity, and terminal-delivery assertions had not yet been reached. Source inspection found one-second polling around asynchronous persistence/admission; the historical delay or rejection cause remains unproven.

A [single secretless AWS replay](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2f09a1a9b741b947886c57916f58b143) used the **actual CI merge `68d7384bcdd499efdae3163188bb45bde3839d7b`**, unchanged complete failing-group manifests, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0, plan concurrency 1 and max workers 2. **All 7,669 tests passed; 10 skipped; no reported failures or unhandled errors.** Command wall time: 32m3.499s. AWS had 32 CPUs/approximately 66 GB RAM versus CI’s 2 CPUs/approximately 8 GB; this passing replay is not proof of a repair or hardware equivalence. The requested runtime policy was bun-compatible, not evidence that Bun executed these groups.

The new head incorporates main’s `11e376cd584f4f37fc0ea75131cc071b1951b62b`, which replaces hosted-lifecycle polling with actual approval publication and lane settlement. This is a refresh for an identified failed fixture, not an unchanged rerun for green. Other readiness uncertainty is retained; related owner work in #154977 and #155007 was not copied or represented as landed. No timeout, retry, assertion, cleanup safeguard or CI gate was weakened.

### Follow-up fixture repair

The [head `94cdd61` run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35634185220) passed the repaired hosted-lifecycle cases but exposed other fixture-readiness assertions. Canonical main fixes now cover recovery and transcript readiness. The overlapping approval publication, request cleanup and acceptance repairs subsequently landed in [#155111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155111); those owners are adopted rather than duplicated.

The remaining clock fixture was independently replaced by the canonical controlled-clock/native-lock test in [#154486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154486), commit f8da95716559f938fdea64eb4597688f2508859a. Supporting #155105 is therefore fully superseded and is not being merged.

The ancestry-preserving, GitHub-signed refresh to 18c594577588d139b4ac159a328cf17e822101df incorporates those owners. All 24 original paths retain exactly the same introduced/deleted line sets. Integration proof against main 6615891 passed **252 tests across 10 files**, production core/extension and extension-test types, three relevant core-test graphs, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap and diff checks. The initial extension lint invocation used an incorrect config path; the corrected remaining-gates run passed on the same verified source bytes.

The independent integration review reported a cumulative-result-prefix concern. It was retained and adjudicated rather than relabeled clean: direct inspection of the installed Anthropic SDK 0.3.257 producer and its buffered-result path shows per-turn result text, not concatenated prior result envelopes. Existing shared-prefix tests deliberately retain distinct valid answers; prefix clipping would damage that contract.

The [fresh 18c5945 CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35658126244) exposed two additional fixture failures: maintenance released its database before task-notification acknowledgment settled, and backup ownership inherited another test's tokenless scratch directory. The current head uses main's canonical maintenance repair and keeps only the still-needed backup isolation in this PR; neither changes production behavior or suppresses warnings.

- Maintenance now uses main's independently landed delivery-settlement owner from `f469e13c0b8e113cbfeaa92fb5e20247e7e35bad`. The PR's redundant version was removed byte-for-byte during conflict resolution. A controlled delay had reproduced `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED` on the old fixture and passed on the repair; the full file passed 22/22 tests plus coordinator/delivery-lifetime siblings and the relevant type graph ([mechanism proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_694f0f6eba70d1b5f06aff8aebb79731), [final-byte gate](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_647d43d2656aeb4242f533c5f076f8ef)).
- Backup ownership now gives the registry-snapshot fixture its own scratch root. The old fixture reproduced the real legacy-scratch warning while the repaired boundary preserved the foreign scratch and restored the process environment. The repaired ownership file passed 8/8 tests, three sibling files passed 18/18, and infra type, lint, format, line-cap and diff checks passed ([proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d630e93abb0d52b83e3edf66e0a92f06), 23.304-second single-worker file wall time).
- The `475dcb29` hosted run then failed four web-search provider assertions in an unrelated runtime-config shard. The PR did not touch `src/config`; the affected file passed 33/33 alone and the unpatched exact 217-file shard passed on stronger AWS hardware, so that replay did not erase the observed hosted ordering/cache failure. The investigation verified the owner: prepared validation must receive an explicit manifest fixture instead of relying on a discovery mock reaching an already-cached module. Main independently landed that canonical repair in `d3e512906b63ca2ba9107aae99cf648ac817deaa`; the current head adopts main's file byte-for-byte rather than carrying a duplicate. The independently reviewed variant passed the exact 217-file shard (**3,420 passed, 5 skipped**), the config/CLI test type graph, lint, format, line-cap and diff checks ([supporting proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_05b252af220b8fceb917e37b10208906)).
- The `13c4d02b` hosted run then hit the Matrix Doctor fixture's 100,000 ms child-process deadlock guard after the preceding 4,609 browser tests. Commit `9950ed5640aa3a5b664214ed65dbd3f3a9a4c2bd` had migrated the fixture from `spawnSync` to the shared child helper but omitted its explicit 120,000 ms timeout. The final head restores that prior fixture policy. On a 2-CPU Testbox, the focused test passed (71.5-second test wall), and the exact three-group CI specification passed: browser 277 files/4,609 tests, Matrix 11 files/99 tests, and Active Memory 2 files/227 tests ([exact-order proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35675070774)). The one-line repair passed independent P0–P3 review scoped-clean at 0.99 confidence.
- The backup delta and the now-superseded config-fixture variant passed independent P0–P3 review; main's canonical fixture repairs carried their own focused proof and review. A fresh whole-candidate P0–P3 review on the earlier conflict-free tree reported one duplicate-snapshot theory that does not match this path: CLI assistant previews use `onPartialReply`, while completed answers alone enter `blockReplyHandler`, so no buffered completed payload is skipped before the boundary flush.
- Final head `9494018f270a8acb1d7d387fc9f6807b14c347ca` passed [exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35675559715) and the current ClawSweeper review reported no blocking finding. GitHub merged it as `915c6f7ac2c7c1c018e353f2769ecd26995bfd2b`.

No live Telegram/provider run or production Gateway restart/deployment was performed. This is isolated protocol and reply-boundary proof, not a claim of live channel verification. No hostile behavior was identified in the reviewed changes.

<details>
<summary>Single-worker test cost</summary>

Commands: `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Command wall seconds, including pnpm and compilation/import overhead (the captured timestamps use nanoseconds):

| File | Seconds |
| --- | ---: |
| `src/agents/cli-output-stream.test.ts` | 2.39 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.background-work.test.ts` | 32.89 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts` | 13.83 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.test.ts` | 12.76 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-completed.test.ts` | 16.42 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-commentary.test.ts` | 36.84 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts` | 14.19 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-delivery.test.ts` | 11.72 |
| `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts` | 22.10 |

The longer existing runtime fixtures are import-bound and exercise real CLI-to-reply or native stdio composition. New ordering cases use deferred promises, not sleeps or polling. Existing coverage is retained; no baselines, assertions, CI gates, or line caps were weakened. Hosted job durations will be recorded once the current-head run completes.

</details>
